title: Grateful Dead Live at Haight Street on 1968-03-03
lineage: AUD > ?? > CD > EAC > CD Wave > SHN

ai_review.summary: Audience tape of the famed “Flatbed Truck” free show delivers a manic, high‑energy Pigpen blues marathon (Viola Lee, Smokestack Lightning, Lovelight, Hurts Me Too), with rough but listenable recording quality.
ai_review.review: The performance is celebrated for its explosive 21‑minute Viola Lee Blues and extended blues covers that kept the Haight crowd in a frenzy; reviewers repeatedly call it a historic, manic spectacle. The tape is an audience recording made by Steve Brown with a cheap mic and limited battery life, resulting in occasional drop‑outs and modest clarity but still far superior to many early ’68 board tapes.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ≈3.9, with strong praise for the show’s energy and standout jams; recording is noted as imperfect but acceptable, leading to an overall solid 4‑star assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape recorded with a cheap microphone; battery died before the end, causing drop‑outs and limited clarity. Still considered better than other early 1968 board recordings.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Impromptu free concert on Haight Street featuring an extended Pigpen‑centered blues set; the band rode a wave of high crowd energy with long, improvisational jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned as part of the “flatbed” vibe and noted for his freedom‑spirit rather than specific playing details.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for a distinct, magical bass line that stood out during the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted taking over parts of Lovelight; some reviewers felt his contribution was less impressive than Pigpen’s.
